What I can state from memory, all labelled as estimates:
- Global solar PV additions were roughly 450 GW in 2024 (est.), up from roughly 350 GW in 2023 (est.). Both are approximate; check IEA, IRENA or SolarPower Europe for exact values.
- China accounted for well over half of annual additions (est.).
- Module prices fell by roughly half between 2023 and 2024 (est.).

**Cannot be measured from this run:** article volume and window, the monthly series and its direction, tone against the corpus baseline, themes by share, named organisations and people by frequency, placed_pct for geography, critical headlines with date/publisher/url, and source concentration. I will not invent them.

Qualitative expectation (interpretation, not measured): themes likely include deployment records, cost declines, grid and storage integration, tariffs and trade disputes, US policy changes, and manufacturing overcapacity in China. ## Verdict
- Answer: Solar power coverage in the Prism news corpus is large (58,907 articles, 2024-06 to 2026-05 [c1]), rising modestly (late third 1.15x the early third [c1]), and overwhelmingly positive in tone (87.3% positive vs 12.1% negative [c1]). The US and India dominate the places named [c1].
- Decision: Treat solar as a stable, favourably covered topic with growing attention in 2026. Do not use these counts as a measure of deployment or market size.
- Confidence: medium - the volume and tone series are complete for the window, but the window ends 2026-05-31, and place and entity labels cover only part of the articles [c1].
- What would change it: Counts for June to October 2026, and a per-article check of the "critical" flag.

## What the data shows
- Volume: 58,907 articles matching "solar power" from 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31, in mention mode [c1].
- Monthly range: 1,812 (2025-06) to 3,609 (2026-04) [c1].
- Tone: 51,356 positive, 7,140 negative, 361 neutral, so a negative-to-positive ratio of 0.14 against a corpus baseline of 0.58 [c1].
- Themes: energy (24.0% share), business (23.0%), technology (15.5%), environment (6.8%) [c1]. The leading subcategory is solar PV systems (22.3%), followed by community solar (6.6%) and storage (5.3%) [c1].
- Organisations: Enphase Energy (530 articles), NTPC (545), Adani Green Energy (459), Tata Power (340), First Solar (299) [c1]. These are machine-assigned labels, not verified identities [c1].
- People: Gautam Adani (419), Pralhad Joshi (251), Ed Miliband (146), Joe Biden (738) [c1]. "Lorde" (337) and "Charli xcx" (78) are almost certainly name collisions (the song "Solar Power"). That is my interpretation and has not been checked per article.
- Critical headlines: the call returned none, so I cannot give dated headlines with publisher and URL [c1]. The "critical" flag covers 45,058 articles (76.5% by my arithmetic from [c1]). That share is high enough that the flag probably does not mean negative. Its meaning is not defined in the response, so I do not interpret it.
- Source concentration: in a sample of 216 articles, the top publisher (renewablesnow.com) held 7.9% and the top three held 16.2%, across 131 publishers [c1]. Coverage is spread widely.

## Trend
The series is flat to modestly rising. The early third totals 19,109 articles and the late third 21,933, a ratio of 1.15 [c1]. The tool reports a compound annual growth rate of 22.0% but labels the direction "flat" [c1]. The jump from 2,419 in 2026-01 to 3,146 in 2026-02 [c1] is the clearest step.

```prism-chart
{"id":"monthly_articles","kind":"line","title":"Monthly articles mentioning solar power","unit":"articles","window":{"from":"2024-06-01","to":"2026-05-31"},"x":{"field":"period","type":"temporal"},"series":[{"name":"articles","source":"call:news.overview#1","points":[["2024-06",2050],["2024-07",2498],["2024-08",2304],["2024-09",2438],["2024-10",2373],["2024-11",2599],["2024-12",2218],["2025-01",2629],["2025-02",2493],["2025-03",2352],["2025-04",2406],["2025-05",1958],["2025-06",1812],["2025-07",2315],["2025-08",2257],["2025-09",2272],["2025-10",2194],["2025-11",2200],["2025-12",2313],["2026-01",2419],["2026-02",3146],["2026-03",3051],["2026-04",3609],["2026-05",3001]]}],"caption":"Volume was flat through 2025, then stepped up from February 2026.","supports":"The series is flat to modestly rising."}
```

## Comparison
Baseline: the corpus-wide ratio of negative to positive articles is 0.58 [c1]. Solar power's ratio is 0.14 [c1]. That is a delta of 0.44, or 0.24 times the baseline [c1]. Solar is therefore far more positively covered than ordinary news. The monthly ratio peaked at 0.25 in 2024-11 and 0.21 in 2025-08 [c1].

## Geography
Placed share: only 59.6% of matched articles carry a place (33,303 of 55,906) [c1]. All shares below are of placed articles, and the place is the one the article is about, not where it was published [c1].

| Country | Articles | Share of placed |
|---|---|---|
| United States | 15,199 | 21.9% |
| India | 10,513 | 15.1% |
| China | 4,128 | 5.9% |
| United Kingdom | 3,537 | 5.1% |
| Australia | 2,823 | 4.1% |

Source: [c1]. India is over-represented relative to the corpus (lift 2.3), as are Germany (2.5) and Nigeria (2.0) [c1]. Low-count rows with high lift should be distrusted because of acronym collisions [c1].

## Drill-down
Layers are the call's own breakdowns: theme categories, subcategories, tags, taxonomy, organisations, people, countries and publishers [c1].

```prism-calls

{"id":"c1","feature":"news.overview","used_for":"all figures","args":{"term":"solar power","since":"2024-06-01"}},
```


## Method and limits
- Window: 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31. This is 145 days before today (2026-10-23), so June to October 2026 is not covered [c1]. Ingest policy censors the newest month [c1].
- Lane: news only. No research or other sources were consulted.
- Match mode: "mention" for trends, tone, themes and places. "entity_central" for publishers and recent articles [c1]. The mention counts include articles that name solar power only in passing.
- Entity and place enrichment is incomplete. Labels past 2026-05-01 are not yet written, and May 2026 fill was about 4% [c1]. The geography and entity windows therefore end 2026-04-30.
- The source-concentration figure rests on a sample of 216 of 300 requested articles [c1].
- What the counts are not: they measure article volume, not installed capacity, investment or prices.
- Interpretation (mine): the "flat" direction, the Lorde and Charli xcx collisions, and the reading of "critical".
- Cannot answer: dated critical headlines (none returned), the identity of individual articles behind the spikes, and any period after May 2026.

## References
No external references were used. All figures come from call c1 (news.overview, Prism, 2026).

## Verdict

- **Answer:** Coverage of “solar power” was broadly flat across the measured window, with a late-period pickup; classified coverage was markedly more positive than ordinary news. Reporting centered on energy and business, with the United States and India most often named as places.
- **Decision:** Use this as a signal of sustained, generally favorable news attention—not as evidence of deployment, investment returns, public opinion, or company performance.
- **Confidence:** medium - the main trends are measured across the full window, but entity and place labels are machine assigned, and the latest month is censored.
- **What would change it:** A complete post-May series, article-level validation of labels, or independent deployment and market data.

## What the data shows

Prism counted **58,907 articles** mentioning “solar power” from **2024-06-01 through 2026-05-31** [c1]. Its match mode is *mention*, so this measures news coverage, not only articles primarily about solar. The full months show a fluctuating series and a late pickup: the final full month had **3,001 articles**, versus **2,050** in the first [c1].

Tone skews positive under Prism’s article-level polarity labels: **87.3% positive**, **12.1% negative**, and **0.6% neutral** [c1]. The negative-to-positive ratio was **0.14**, against a corpus baseline of **0.58** [c1]. This is a classifier reading, not a measure of public sentiment.

Among labelled themes, energy and business dominate by volume; solar PV, community solar, and storage stand out among subcategories [c1]. Organisation labels include Enphase Energy, Adani Green Energy, Tata Power, NTPC, and First Solar; person labels include Gautam Adani and Pralhad Joshi [c1]. These are machine-assigned co-occurrences, not verified prominence or affiliation.

## Trend

The monthly series rises from **2,050** articles in the first full month to **3,001** in the last, while Prism characterizes the overall direction as flat; the late third contains **15%** more articles than the early third [c1]. The apparent endpoint increase is therefore not a smooth month-by-month rise. April 2026 peaked at **3,609** [c1].


## Comparison

The comparison is negative-to-positive article ratio: solar coverage’s **0.14** is **0.44 lower**, or about **76% lower**, than the corpus baseline of **0.58** [c1]. Baseline is ordinary news coverage in Prism’s corpus; the comparison uses the same ratio definition. It does not establish that readers or the public feel positive about solar.

## Geography

The geography panel places **59.6%** of matched articles; its denominator is **55,906** matched articles, of which **33,303** were placed [c1]. Place means the country an article is about, not where it was published. Among placed coverage, the United States leads (**15,199** articles; **21.9%**), followed by India (**10,513**; **15.1%**) and China (**4,128**; **5.9%**) [c1]. Placement is incomplete and machine resolved, so these shares do not describe all coverage or solar activity in those countries.

## Drill-down

Reporting labels point to energy, business, technology, sustainability, and environment; subcategory labels include PV systems, shared solar, storage, and grid integration [c1]. Organisation and person rankings have not been independently validated. Prism returned no critical-headline records in its critical feed, so this source set cannot identify critical headlines with dates, publishers, and URLs. Publisher concentration is sampled, not window-wide: the sample contained **216** articles from **131** publishers; the top publisher accounted for **7.9%** and the top three for **16.2%** [c1].
